scenes.headline: SQL Queries
scenes.subtitle: Using Spark SQL alongside the DataFrame API.
scenes.narration: Spark SQL lets you express transformations in standard SQL, which the same engine optimizes as DataFrame code.

scenes.headline: Why use SQL
items: Familiar syntax for analysts and engineers
Runs through the same Catalyst optimizer
Mix freely with the DataFrame API
Great for complex joins and aggregations
scenes.narration: SQL offers familiar syntax for both analysts and engineers. It runs through the same Catalyst optimizer as DataFrames, mixes freely with the DataFrame API, and shines for complex joins and aggregations.

scenes.headline: A SQL query over a view
scenes.code:
df.createOrReplaceTempView("orders")

top = spark.sql("""
    SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS orders
    FROM orders
    GROUP BY customer_id
    HAVING COUNT(*) > 5
""")
scenes.narration: After registering the orders view, we run a SQL query that counts orders per customer and uses HAVING to keep only customers with more than five. The engine plans and optimizes this exactly as it would the equivalent DataFrame code.

scenes.headline: SQL vs DataFrame API
scenes.narration: Spark SQL is declarative and concise, ideal for aggregations, while the DataFrame API is programmatic and easier to build dynamically. Both compile to the same optimized plan, so choose whichever reads more clearly.

scenes.text: SQL and DataFrames are interchangeable — pick the clearer style for each task.
scenes.narration: Because SQL and DataFrames compile to the same plan, pick whichever style reads more clearly for the task at hand.
